nodes.description: The non-MMR entry point into the Lynch pathograph. A germline monoallelic deletion of the 3' end of EPCAM removes its polyadenylation signal; transcription reads through and the MSH2 promoter 15 kb downstream is inactivated by hypermethylation. The deleted region acts in cis on MSH2 rather than through loss of EPCAM's own function, so this node is modelled separately from the coding-variant route while feeding the same mismatch repair defect. MSH2 inactivation is reported specifically in cell lineages that express EPCAM.

biological_processes: epigenetic silencing of the MSH2 promoter

evidence.reference_title: EPCAM deletion carriers constitute a unique subgroup of Lynch syndrome patients.
evidence.snippet: These patients carry deletions of the 3' end of the EPCAM gene, including its polyadenylation signal. Due to concomitant transcriptional read-through of EPCAM, the promoter of MSH2 15 kb further downstream becomes inactivated through hypermethylation.

evidence.reference_title: EPCAM deletion carriers constitute a unique subgroup of Lynch syndrome patients.
